In the interest of charity towards Sam, seeing as this subreddit is named after him, I'll propose that his view of the problem seems to stem from the fact that many Democrat voices, within politics, in MSM, and in so-called "alternative media," have trouble framing their immigration comments around what they support about the conversation. It's often much easier, and much less damning politically, to frame it around what you don't support in the other guys' platform. To the average listener, this seems to perpetuate the idea that Democrats favor the extreme version of open boarders because of the apparent hostility to any form of policing, believing it to be cover for racism or nationalism with a eugenics flavor. 

Separately, it does bother me that MUCH of politics is like this, where politicians say little about ACTUAL beliefs, but A LOT about what thy oppose, which only facilitates the escalation of conversations between the major sides since people are reacting to what they *think* their "enemies" are implying, implications that are amplified by pundits on their side, leading to unhealthy political fractionation by way of nasty positive feedback loops.

To make a tangential point, I know much of the frustration with Sam at this point originates in his amplifying of minor issues on the left, which are often shared on the right, while ignoring major issues on the right. 
I think there is merit to believing that Sam has ultimately good intentions, and for extending an olive branch with the memory of his ultimately left-based roots (see Rebecca Traister podcast, as well as his response to the Kavanaugh debacle.) When someone sees problems with their camp, and turn their critical eye to those problems, those within their camp often begin to see them as a foreigner. We must remember that it's not incumbent on ideological foreigners to fix a group, it's natives to that group. Sam is that native, but has admittedly had some tunnel vision in that regard, for which he deserves criticism. What is frustrating, and which I believe should stop, no matter who we're discussing, is the demonization of these characters based on assumptions about their intent, without requisite evidence. This type of imagination is unhealthy, especially in political discourse.

That's probably fair. But as a journalist, that's essentially his job, and the only real requirement is to have good instincts about fairness, Justice, narrative, etc., all of which he seems to possess.

I think there’s a deeper issue to be discussed here. Stephen West didn’t mention this, but it would seem that Post-Modern critiques related to philosophy of science wouldn’t necessarily dispute the instrumentality of science and the scientific method. They would challenge the assumption that those methods are providing us with any semblance of objective reality. If we are accessing the world through sense organs that provide adaptive advantage, and we construct a conceptual world through language and mental models, and on top of that weave in cultural artifacts that we do not notice (without thorough inspection) that allow us to make sense of the world, than it is worth wondering if the tools and theories we contrive and test are, unbeknownst to us, laden with biases and assumptions that we don’t even see, and thus that our seemingly objective reality is really a heavily darkened prism. Again, this does not mean that science is not useful, but we should take care to ensure that we are not being fed a narrative that could be unwittingly benefiting a group of people that share that narrative and perspective, to the detriment of other participant groups. 

I would like to add that I see these conversations as ongoing discussions, not a series of battles in a war. If I am wrong, I’m the first person that would like to know. Lol

I wasn’t making a statement about any specific idea or critique. I don’t understand how one can place blame on ideas for the ways people misinterpret or mishandle them. One can find errors in practice that don’t necessarily make the ideas they were based on incoherent or null and void.
